extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to RCE via Jinja2 Template().render() on user input — Remote code execution: an attacker can run arbitrary Python and OS shell commands on the host/container, fully compromising the application, its secrets, and network position. [verified: User-controlled `name` (line 19) is f-string interpolated into `content` (line 38) then passed to `Template(content).render()` (line 41) with no SandboxedEnvironment, so `{{...}}` payloads execute arbitrary Python/OS commands.]

Hardcoded secret token/credentials in source code — Exposed secret token grants any attacker reading the source or container image the credentials, enabling impersonation/authentication to whatever the token protects. [verified: app/config.py lines 13 and 15 assign literal secret values ("John Ripper", "5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n") instead of the intended os.getenv, and they are committed in source and even duplicated in README.md, so anyone with repo/image read access obtains them. Severity is medium since the token has no enforced auth use in this demo app (only used as a default name), but it is a genuinely present insecure sett]

Debug mode enabled exposes verbose error pages — Verbose tracebacks leak source code, file paths, and runtime state to remote attackers, aiding exploitation (e.g., refining the SSTI/RCE payload). [verified: `debug=config.DEBUG` (line 14) is wired to the DEBUG env var which defaults to True in deployment (`.env_temp` sets DEBUG=True), so Starlette returns full tracebacks/source to anonymous clients on unhandled exceptions.]

Outbound HTTP request without timeout (DoS) — A hanging or slow external endpoint blocks request workers indefinitely, exhausting resources and making the app unavailable. [verified: app/main.py:32 calls requests.get(PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL) with no timeout; in this async def route the blocking call stalls the event loop, and a hung upstream causes app-wide DoS with no compensating timeout control present.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped reflection of name and external IP into HTML — Attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in victims' browsers, enabling session theft, credential phishing, and client-side actions in the app's origin. [verified: `name` and untrusted `public_ip_response.text` are concatenated unescaped into HTML returned as the response (lines 36-41) with no output encoding, allowing `<script>` injection reflected to the browser.]
